background: Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks, the holding company of Mizuho Bank and Mizuho Securities, funded by a very large base of yen deposits and lending to Japanese corporates and households and to large companies worldwide.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the group, at A- on average, both on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 17 Sep 2015, so the grades have been steady for a decade. The ratios are on the weak side of Asian peers across the board: CET1 of 13.5% is below the peer median, leverage of 4.9% is in the bottom quarter, and LCR of 126% and NSFR of 112% are both in the bottom quarter. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The flagged news is good, with first-quarter profit up 45.5% reported on 31 Jul 2026. A systemically important Japanese name running thinner ratios than most Asian peers.
